# Authentic v0.1.40 transaction participation predecessor

`predecessor.lkja` and `predecessor.lkjp` were produced by the anonymously acquired official
v0.1.40 executable using public operations outside the compiler checkout. They retain the exact
old standard and separately transported typed-cell library closure. They are original bytes,
not a current-runtime reconstruction. `provenance.json` binds the executable, source and package
identities; the runtime executable itself remains in ignored campaign evidence.

`producer.request` contains the unchanged maintained transaction-owning `try-update` algorithm
from `requirements.producer.structural.lkjc` at main `868e55c73c7f14fbbb2387f39c67290ed0122cd1`.
`consumer.request` adds a native ordinary raw helper, independently authored read-only observer,
and three targets. The two transaction owners use public structural expression blocks because
v0.1.40 rejects native declaration-unit `transaction-outcome` and cannot draft its own accepted
transaction body. The original native request and both genuine diagnostics are preserved.

Before execution, the expectations were fixed: an empty store; same-canonical owner reentry
fails with `normalized_transaction_nested`; no data or HEAD change; raw helper adjustments of
-30 and -10 under one ancestor owner start from fallback 100 and return `Committed(60)`;
a separate process reads `[60]`; exactly one physical data revision was added. The authentic
`official-*.stdout` files record these observations. `expected.json` is their independent oracle.
`read-credit.deployment.json` is the original descriptor; the maintained runner substitutes only
its artifact basename and target when launching fresh disposable stores.

The current reader stages the exact old transport, executes the exact old artifact, preserves
the old nested-owner rejection, and independently reopens the store to compare complete I64
encoding bytes and HEAD. This proves compatibility with old exact dependencies and confirms
that raw participation already existed. It does not establish the new guarded library workflow,
which has its own maintained composition witness.

`new-guard.lkja` contains the newly authored ordinary caller and standard library, using the
unchanged artifact encoding. It was authored natively by a copied intermediate campaign executable against
the exact new standard transport. Its caller supplies `get`, `put` and `require-transaction` and
calls `data-cell-update-in-transaction` with a callback that would divide by zero. The official
v0.1.40 executable rejects this artifact's deployment with capability `normalized_data_operation`
for `require-transaction`, exit 3, before reading its deliberately unavailable secret or opening its
absent data root. `new-guard-provenance.json`, the original descriptor, literal request and exact
old-runtime stdout/exit preserve that observation. The receipt reader admits the exact retained
artifact and requires the original unsupported-operation diagnostic; it does not fetch an old
runtime or label this retained proof as a fresh candidate execution. Artifact substitution and
replacing the diagnostic with a later secret failure are rejected by its adversarial reader test.
